# Diversified receive encryption fixtures

These are public, synthetic test values. They are not wallet credentials and must
never be used as real recovery material.

`shielded-receive-encryption.reference.js` is a test-only implementation. It uses
noble Ristretto arithmetic and independently implements RFC 9380 XMD expansion,
the application framing, SHA-512 scalar reduction, HKDF and AES-GCM with Node
crypto. It imports no production protocol helpers. Production secret arithmetic
uses the separate libsodium WASM backend; this reference must not be replaced by
a call to that backend.

`shielded-receive-encryption.vectors.json` freezes three deterministic examples,
including intermediate values, empty inputs, high-bit inputs, UTF-8 and binary
plaintext, and a 512-byte ciphertext. They were generated by the reference and
checked against the pre-WASM production implementation before migrating the
secret arithmetic backend. Tests check the frozen values; they do not silently
regenerate them. An intentional protocol revision can regenerate them with:

```sh
node packages/protocol-core/test/fixtures/generate-shielded-receive-vectors.mjs
```

`ristretto255-invalid-encodings.json` copies all 29 invalid Ristretto encodings
from [RFC 9496 Appendix A.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9496.html#appendix-A.2).
Tests also reject the valid encoding of the identity, which is prohibited by this
application protocol. The RFC input set and the additional identity rule are
separate requirements.

`ristretto255-rfc-vectors.json` copies published values that do not depend on
this protocol: the seven `expand_message_xmd(SHA-512)` vectors of
[RFC 9380 Appendix K.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9380.html#appendix-K.3),
the seven element-derivation vectors of
[RFC 9496 Appendix A.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9496.html#appendix-A.3)
and the generator multiples of
[RFC 9496 Appendix A.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9496.html#appendix-A.1).
Tests run them against the production noble expansion and the libsodium WASM map
and multiplication. They anchor the composed hash-to-group and point
multiplication to the standards, not only to the reference implementation above.

Run the fixed vectors, cross-implementation properties, invalid encodings and
deterministic mutation corpus with:

```sh
node --test packages/protocol-core/test/shielded-receive-encryption-vectors.test.js
```

The normal protocol-core test command includes this file. These checks detect
specific regressions and provide independently reproducible interoperability
evidence; they do not constitute an independent audit, a formal security proof,
or a guarantee of constant-time execution in every browser.
